title: Department Mandate, Legal Limits & Civilian Agency Standing
content:
The San Andreas Department of Transportation (SADOT) operates as an official public works and incident management agency under the State of San Andreas Civilian Department. Our operational mission is to preserve roadway infrastructure, protect emergency scenes, maintain statewide transit flow, and deliver immersive, high-quality public service roleplay.

Official Department Motto"Preserving Infrastructure, Protecting the Traveling Public."
⚠️ Absolute Statutory Limitations & Zero Peace Officer Powers

SADOT personnel are strictly civilian civil service workers. Personnel hold zero law enforcement, peace officer, or arrest authority under state penal codes. Crossing these legal boundaries is treated as severe Fail RP and triggers immediate termination. Personnel are prohibited from:

  • Conducting Traffic Stops: Personnel shall never pull over, box in, or initiate an enforcement stop against any moving civilian vehicle.
  • Engaging in Pursuits: Never follow, chase, or conduct PIT maneuvers against fleeing or suspect vehicles. Report descriptions over radio and clear the roadway.
  • Detaining or Searching Civilians: Personnel have no legal power to detain, frisk, handcuff, or interrogate any individual. Vehicle searches are exclusive to LEO.
  • Carrying Lethal Firearm Hardware: Carrying or brandishing firearms while on duty or operating a state vehicle is strictly prohibited.
Authorized Operational Scope
  • Establishing highway tapers, detours, and protective vehicle blocks.
  • Clearing disabled, wrecked, or impounded vehicles via rollbacks and wreckers.
  • Emergency roadside assist (flat tires, battery jumpstarts, 1–2 gal fuel).
  • Debris extraction, hazardous chemical/fluid containment, and infrastructure repairs.
  • Providing tactical illumination and scene shielding for Police, Fire, and EMS.
Core Department Standards
  • Roleplay Depth: Walk to truck beds, interact with tools, and roleplay realistic mechanical repairs. Instant menu repairs are prohibited.
  • Safety Over Assets: Human life always takes priority over equipment or road reopening deadlines.
  • Inter-Agency Decorum: Treat allied agencies (SAMPD, BCSO, SAFR) with absolute professional courtesy.
  • No Personal Pets: To maintain strict workplace safety, personal pets are barred from duty rigs.

title: Department Structure, Chain of Command & Scene Authority
content:
SADOT operates under a structured Chain of Command to maintain operational integrity, clear communications, and safe coordination on major emergency scenes.

Unified Scene Command & Authority Transfer

On active emergency scenes with allied first responders (Police, Sheriff, Fire, EMS), the primary responding Law Enforcement Officer or Fire Scene Commander holds absolute Scene Command. Arriving SADOT operators must stage 25–50 feet back along the shoulder, remain with their vehicle, and await instructions. SADOT shall not alter barricades, hook vehicles, or clear debris until the Scene Commander officially releases the area. Once released, command over roadway reopening and traffic management transfers to the senior on-scene SADOT unit.

Command Staff (Commissioner / Deputy / Chief of Ops)Directs department policy, command appointments, fleet procurement, and high-level inter-agency liaison.
DOT-001 – DOT-003
Supervisory Staff (Manager / Supervisor)Manages on-duty shift deployment, field evaluations, major lane closure approvals, and equipment red-tags.
DOT-004 – DOT-007
Field Operators (Senior Operator / Operator II / Operator I)Qualified technicians authorized for solo patrol, flatbed towing, highway incident clearing, and infrastructure repairs.
DOT-100 – DOT-300
Probationary Operator (Cadet)New recruit undergoing field evaluation. Restricted to utility rigs and must patrol with an assigned FTO or Supervisor.
DOT-400 Series

title: Personnel Conduct, Activity Minimums & Disciplinary Framework
content:
Personnel represent the State of San Andreas at all times. Operators are expected to maintain active service standing, adhere to reporting baselines, and maintain professional decorum.

Monthly Activity Baseline (3 Hours)

All active roster members must record at least three (3) verified patrol hours per calendar month via the official Patrol Log. Failure to fulfill this quota results in immediate reassignment to Inactive Status and revocation of vehicle access keys pending command review.

Probationary 14-Day Window

Cadets must complete their practical evaluations with an FTO or Supervisor within 14 calendar days of roster sign-up. Cadets failing to schedule or clear training within 14 days will be automatically dropped from the active personnel roster.

The Progressive Three-Strike Policy
STRIKE 1: Formal WarningIssued for minor procedural lapses (messy depot return, low fuel tank, uniform texture errors). Active on record for 30 days.
STRIKE 2: Suspension & FreezeIssued for repeat violations, careless driving, or unprofessional conduct. Triggers 1–3 day suspension and a 30-day promotion lock.
STRIKE 3: Command ReviewIssued for chronic policy failures. Results in immediate key revocation and administrative board review for demotion or termination.
Immediate Termination Offenses (Bypasses Strike System):Severe Fail RP, abusing scripts or spawning barriers to troll players, performing traffic stops, carrying lethal weapons, insubordination, or using fleet apparatus off-duty for criminal RP results in instant blacklisting.

title: Radio Communications, Brevity & Phonetic Standards
content:
Department radio frequencies are monitored by state dispatchers and allied agencies. Operators must keep radio traffic strictly operational, concise, and structured according to standardized 10-code brevity.

10-4Acknowledged
10-6Busy / Standby
10-7Out of Service
10-8In Service / Available
10-9Repeat Message
10-19Return to Depot
10-20Location
10-23Arrived on Scene
10-33Scene Clear
10-41Beginning Shift
10-42Ending Shift
10-76En Route
Mandatory Location Callout Syntax:

"[Unit Callsign] to Dispatch, 10-23 at [Nearest Map Postal Code], [Primary Highway or Intersection], establishing safety buffer."

Example: "DOT-102 to Dispatch, 10-23 at Postal 402 on Olympic Freeway at Las Lagunas, staging lane 1 arrow buffer."

title: Fleet Equipment, Paintwork & Vehicle Authorization Policy
content:
Every in-service apparatus represents the State of San Andreas. Custom performance upgrades, neon underglow, aftermarket sports rims, wraps, and unauthorized body work are strictly prohibited.

Fleet Visual Identity Standards
  • Mandatory Paint: Solid Orange (Color Code 24, Metallic) across all primary and secondary panels.
  • Official State Plate: License plates must read SA DOT. Driving on personal civilian plates is an equipment violation.
  • Window Tint: Tint must remain stock clear or light smoke. Dark limousine blackout tint is completely prohibited for driver safety and visibility.
  • Commercial Wheels: Rims must remain standard commercial, industrial, or heavy utility wheels.
Rank & Certification Authorization
  • Cadet+: Restricted to Chevy Tahoe (civtahoe).
  • Operator I+: Dodge Ram 3500 HD (civramdot1), Ford F550 Rollback 1.5 (f550rollback1).
  • Senior Operator+: Arrow Board Rigs (civf550dot, civramdot2).
  • Supervisor+ / HVY Cert: Heavy Wreckers (kenworthwrecker), Lowboy tractor (w900).
vMenu Extra ConfigurationsOperators must enable all required lightbar and equipment extras prior to departing any depot. Refer to the internal Vehicle Guidelines portal for exact extra combinations.

title: Life-Safety, Scene Staging & Emergency Disengagement
content:
Technician life-safety supersedes state equipment, vehicles, or road reopening deadlines at all times. Operators have the full authority to pause or evacuate an unsafe work zone.

Active Threat & Armed Altercation Retreat Protocol (10-99)

If weapons are drawn, shots are fired, or an active criminal threat breaks out within or adjacent to an active work zone, personnel must execute immediate emergency disengagement:

1. STOPCease winching or paving work instantly.
2. DROP GEARLeave cones, tools, and cables on the road.
3. EVACUATERun or drive away to a secure area.
4. CALL 911Radio "10-99" with postal, wait for LEO Code 4.
The 50-Foot Powerline Rule

Always assume downed electrical wires are energized and lethal. Maintain a strict 50-foot standoff perimeter. Block all approaching lanes with barricades and never drive vehicles over wires.

Mandatory Cabin Clearance

Never tilt a rollback bed or actuate any winch line while a civilian or emergency responder is inside the vehicle. Visually confirm the vehicle cabin is 100% empty before winching.

title: Shift Documentation & Subdivision Field Training Mandates
content:
Accountability ensures transparency and state equipment maintenance. Every operational deployment, tow transport, and patrol hour must be documented on official state portals prior to logging off duty.

Patrol Shift Log

Must be submitted at the conclusion of every shift to register active patrol hours, callsign activity, and post-shift depot checklist compliance.

Master Field Ops (MFO) Log

Mandatory for every vehicle tow, flatbed transport, tire change, fuel delivery, road closure, and equipment movement executed on shift.

Central Dispatch Work Orders

Operators attached to central dispatch tickets must update ticket status from En Route (10-76) to Resolved (10-33) once coordinates are clear.

Subdivision Field Training Academy Notice

In compliance with Board of Directors directives, all step-by-step game controls, geometric taper spacing rules, /traffic node configurations, trailer loading scripts (/attach), and practical FTO sign-off rubrics have been placed in the internal Subdivision Training Academy portal. Operators must consult that manual for hands-on operational instructions.

"Preserving Infrastructure, Protecting the Traveling Public."

title: Civilian Property, Tow Disputes & Release-on-Scene Policy
content:
Towing interactions frequently involve distressed citizens. Personnel must enforce state custody standards calmly, transparently, and with full pre-tow documentation.

Pre-Hookup Inspection & Photo RP

Before hooking J-hooks or bridle straps to any vehicle, operators must conduct a 360-degree walkaround documenting pre-existing body damage, cracked glass, or missing tires on their tablet. This protects state employees against false property damage claims.

The "Release-on-Scene" Standard

If a registered owner arrives on scene before the recovery rig departs with the casualty secured on the deck: for routine disabled or parking calls, personnel may release the vehicle on scene once property ownership is verified and a waiver is signed.

⚠️ Police Impound Release ProhibitionIf a vehicle is being impounded under Law Enforcement authority (Evidentiary Hold, Seizure, Driver Arrested), personnel are strictly barred from releasing the vehicle on scene under any circumstances. Advise the owner to resolve the hold directly with the requesting police agency (SAMPD or BCSO).

title: High-Visibility PPE & Strict Tactical Gear Ban
content:
Personnel must maintain a clean, recognizable civilian public works appearance. Operating without mandatory reflective safety gear, or attempting to dress like armed tactical police is strictly prohibited.

Mandatory Roadway PPE
  • ANSI Class 3 Safety Vests/Jackets: High-visibility orange or lime-yellow reflective vests must be worn anytime personnel step outside a vehicle onto a roadway or shoulder.
  • Safety Hard Hats: Required on active bridge works, culvert excavations, tree felling, and heavy machinery sites.
  • Work Boots: Steel-toed work boots must be worn on all field shifts.
Strict Ban on Tactical Police Gear
  • No Body Armor / Plate Carriers: Heavy tactical vests, external armor carriers, and Kevlar vests are completely banned.
  • No Police Duty Belts: Handcuff pouches, taser holsters, magazine pouches, and drop-leg tactical rigs are banned.
  • No SWAT / Combat Helmets: Military helmets, gas masks, and balaclavas are strictly prohibited.

title: Leave of Absence (LOA) & Inactive Roster Protection
content:
The department provides formal Leave of Absence protections to ensure personnel do not forfeit rank, callsigns, or active standing during scheduled personal leaves or examinations.

LOA Duration & Approval Thresholds
  • Up to 14 Calendar Days: May be approved directly by any on-duty Supervisor or Manager.
  • 15 to 30 Calendar Days: Requires formal filing and sign-off by Command Staff.
  • Extensions: Any leave exceeding 30 continuous days requires Executive Review.
Standing & Inactivity Protections
  • Monthly Quota Exemption: Approved LOAs fully exempt personnel from the 3-hour monthly patrol baseline.
  • Credential Hold: Callsign, certified rank, and subdivision training accesses remain locked and protected.
  • Unexcused Inactivity: Inactivity exceeding 45 days without an approved LOA results in administrative roster pruning.
